1938, July 18
The following is a faithful transcription of the type written original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O.F.M. Cap.
VILLA AND FEAST OF ST. VINCENT £ BRIGHTON, MICHIGAN July 18, 1938
Mr. James M. Casey 124 Warren Ave. Seattle, Wash.
My dear Brother James :
God bless you and all yours -- and sure including my poor self in every blessing I can get or give. Thanks be to God for the Faith and for all His blessings.
I had Fr. Edward with me at the Monastary nearly 2 months to June 18th. Back from the Philippines, as you know, he was doing real missionary work for religion in the "Far East" something over the 12 months he was here. He seemed to enjoy his stay at St. Bonaventure's. I certainly did. Shortly after leaving Detroit and back to his headquarters in St. Paul, he received information from his Bishop in the Philippines that he is expected back there in September. It is possible that he may not be able to get this way again before his voyage west- ward.
Musing together over the celebration of his Jubilee, and the triple vacation it occasioned us, we agreed that it were theme enough for a little treatise of some kind, whereby to praise the wonderful ways of God's providence, and at the same time, offer an expression of appreciation to the many dear ones -- old and new -- and for the gratitude we all experienced at so many manifestations of kindness at their hands.
Details of preparations for that celebration, at least the more remote, will hardly be necessary or expected here. As the Senior of the family -- since dear Ella passed away -- you know those details; having watched the career of each of us longer and perhaps with more interest than anyone else breathing to- day. Something the same might be said also to poor, dear Brother Pat, and, for that matter, though of course with shorter scope of vision back to earlier spring-time of life, to each of the others -- Guss and Owen, and the one-time three little sisters -- now we might say Grandmas -- Margaret, Grace and Mayme.
I am not certain if I ever wrote you of Fr. Maurice Joachim's Jubilee in New York. It was suppose to take place just a year ahead of Fr. Edward's. Anyhow, they sent me thither to help
